chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Inform me about the Will from God and from creation.' So he said: 'The Will from creation is the inner resolve, and what then manifests from them in action. But as for the Will from God the Exalted, His Will is His act of bringing into being — nothing other than that — because He does not deliberate, nor does He have whims, nor does He think; and these attributes are negated from Him, for they are the attributes of creation.'

So the Will of God is the act itself, nothing other than that. He says to it: Be! — and it is — without a spoken word, without utterance by a tongue, without a whim, without thought, and without any modality for that, just as there is no modality for Him.

key_terms.إِحْدَاثُهُ: His bringing into being — the divine creative act identical with the divine Will
key_terms.الضَّمِيرُ: Inner conscience/resolve — the internal psychological state of intent in creatures before action
key_terms.الْإِرَادَةُ: Will/Intention — the central term of this hadith, distinguished between creaturely psychological will and divine creative will
key_terms.كَيْفَ: Modality/'how' — the absolute negation of any quantitative or qualitative description of God's Will
key_terms.مَنْفِيَّةٌ: Negated — the theological method of tanzih (divine transcendence) applied to anthropomorphic attributes

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God's Will and human will according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Safwan ibn Yahya, one of the most trusted companions of Imam al-Ridha, posed a profound theological question distinguishing God's Will from creaturely will. The Imam's answer became a cornerstone of Shia rational theology: for creatures, will involves internal deliberation and psychological states before action; for God, will is identical with act — the divine 'Be!' (kun fa-yakun) is instantaneous and without any creaturely mediation or modality.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Inform me about the Intention (Will) from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and from the creature’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Intention from the creature (people) is the conscience and begins for them after that from the deed, and as for (the Intention) from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted, so His<sup>azwj</sup> Intention is His<sup>azwj</sup> Creation and not other than that, because He<sup>azwj</sup> neither narrates, nor whims, nor thinks, and these Attributes are negated from Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and these are the attributes of the creatures.

So the Intention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the deed, not other than that. He<sup>azwj</sup> is Saying to it, ‘Be’, so it occurs (comes into being), without a letter spoken by a tongue, nor a whim, nor thinking, nor is there a ‘where’ for that just as there is no ‘where’ (qualitative state) for Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following.

“I asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.), ‘Enlighten me about the will of Allah and the will of His creatures.’” He said, “The will of His creatures comes from what goes in their minds and leads to action. Will of Allah, the Most High, is His inventing and nothing else because Allah does not need to reflect, deliberate or think. Such qualities do not exist with Him. They are the attributes of His creation.

Allah’s will is His acts and nothing else. He says to it: Be, and it comes into existence, without any words or utterance of the tongue, any inclination and reflection. His will has no conditions just as His self has no conditions.”
